title: Ice Maker Not Producing Ice
shortDescription: Whirlpool ice maker has stopped producing ice despite power being on.
fullDescription:
E1 on Whirlpool standalone and built-in ice makers indicates no ice production. Common culprits are a closed water supply valve, failed water inlet valve, or stuck ice maker module.

Verify water supply first, then work through electrical components.

fixSteps.title: Check supply
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure the water supply saddle valve is open.

fixSteps.title: Test inlet valve
fixSteps.instruction: Measure continuity on the solenoid and verify 120V at the connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace module
fixSteps.instruction: Unscrew ice maker module and swap with replacement.

whenToCallPro: If both the inlet valve and module test fine but ice maker still fails.

faq.a: Yes - a clogged filter can reduce water flow below threshold.

title: Ice Maker Sensor Error
shortDescription: Temperature or optical sensor on the ice maker not responding.
fullDescription:
E2 indicates a sensor issue - either the ice bin optical sensor fails to see the emitter, or the thermistor reports a shorted/open value.

Clean the emitter/receiver lenses and inspect the harness.

fixSteps.title: Clean sensors
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe optical emitter and receiver lenses with a soft damp cloth.

fixSteps.title: Check harness
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect sensor wiring for breaks or loose connectors.

whenToCallPro: If sensor replacement does not clear the code.
videoSearchQuery: Whirlpool E2 ice maker optical sensor

faq.a: Mounted on either side of the ice bucket housing in the freezer.

title: Power Outage Notification
fullDescription:
PO (or PF on older models) flashes after a power outage. The ice maker resumes automatically but the notification stays until acknowledged.

Press any button to clear. Check ice in bin for melt-refreeze.

fixSteps.title: Acknowledge
fixSteps.instruction: Press any button on the control panel to clear.

fixSteps.title: Empty bucket
fixSteps.instruction: Discard any melted or clumped ice.

faq.a: If temperature stayed below 40F and freezer below 0F, yes.

title: Water Filter Replacement
fullDescription:
Whirlpool fridges use EveryDrop filters (EDR1RXD1 and variants). The indicator turns red at 6 months or 200 gallons.

Replace and reset with the filter button.

fixSteps.title: Replace filter
fixSteps.instruction: Push button to eject; insert new filter and push until it clicks.

fixSteps.title: Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Hold Filter Reset button for 3 seconds.

faq.a: Check existing filter - EDR1RXD1, EDR2RXD1, EDR3RXD1, or EDR4RXD1.

title: Ice Fan Error
shortDescription: Ice compartment fan not running properly.
fullDescription:
Er IF reports a stall in the ice compartment fan. Ice fails to freeze without adequate airflow.

Defrost and inspect the fan.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: Access and swap the ice compartment fan.

whenToCallPro: If defrost does not clear the code.

faq.a: Ice maker will be disabled; rest of fridge works normally.

title: Ice Maker Overfill
shortDescription: Water detected beyond normal fill level.
fullDescription:
E4 triggers when the fill sensor detects water overflow, usually from a stuck inlet valve or damaged fill tube.

Shut off water and inspect the inlet valve.
whenToCallPro: If you suspect a leak behind fridge cabinetry.

faq.a: Yes - act quickly to prevent floor and cabinet damage.

title: Communication Failure
fullDescription:
CF indicates a loss of communication between the UI and main control board. Ice maker commands cannot be issued.

Reseat connectors and power cycle.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cables
fixSteps.instruction: Open UI housing, firmly push connectors into sockets.

whenToCallPro: If reseating does not clear CF, board replacement may be needed.

faq.a: Reseating cables is DIY; board replacement often isn't cost effective.

title: Door Ajar Warning
shortDescription: Freezer or fridge door not fully closed.
fullDescription:
dR indicates the door has been ajar for over 5 minutes. Ice maker pauses to prevent frost buildup.

Close door fully and the code clears.

fixSteps.title: Close door
fixSteps.instruction: Verify door fully seals against gasket.

fixSteps.title: Test switch
fixSteps.instruction: Press switch manually; fridge light should turn off.

whenToCallPro: For gasket replacement if alignment is tricky.

faq.a: The door switch may be stuck or gasket worn, preventing proper closure detection.

title: Sabbath Mode Active
shortDescription: Fridge is in Sabbath mode; ice maker paused.
fullDescription:
SAb shows when Sabbath mode is enabled. Ice maker, dispensers, and some internal functions are disabled until exited.

Hold the appropriate button combination to exit.

fixSteps.title: Exit Sabbath
fixSteps.instruction: Hold Lock + Filter buttons for 4 seconds.

faq.a: Held Lock + Filter for 4 seconds by accident; same combo toggles it off.

title: Evaporator Coil Error
shortDescription: Evaporator coil sensor or defrost issue.
fullDescription:
EC reports a defrost/evaporator thermistor fault. Frost will accumulate and the ice maker will eventually stop.

Replace the thermistor and clear frost via forced defrost.

fixSteps.title: Forced defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Initiate forced defrost per service manual.

faq.a: Yes - heavy frost can crack evaporator fins and stall the fan.

title: Optics Board Fault
shortDescription: Whirlpool ice maker optics emitter/receiver fault.
fullDescription: F2 indicates the emitter or receiver optical board cannot complete its self-test. The optics are used to detect bin level and dispenser activity. Both boards are replaced as a pair on most models.

fixSteps.title: Cycle power
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 5 minutes, restore power and observe.

fixSteps.title: Run service test
fixSteps.instruction: Enter service diagnostics per tech sheet and step through tests.

fixSteps.title: Replace component
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM replacement and clear code.

faq.q: Where is the Whirlpool ice maker tech sheet?
faq.a: Inside the kick plate or behind the lower service panel on most under-counter and built-in models.
